notes:
Account summary: Emberfall operates edge-connected assembly line AI (diagnostics + operator assistant). Looking for dedicated capacity to guarantee throughput for 24/7 inference (safety-critical features). Key asks: 99th percentile latency SLOs for short-chat flows, committed GPU sizing for steady-state + burst, clear unit economics per token for finance signoff.

Key constraints / quotes: "We cannot have model-induced variance during peak shift changeovers" - CTO. Need kms/HSM integration (on-prem) for model keys and audit trail. Data residency: US-only; logs kept 1 year.

POC & perf notes (technical):
- Baseline: internal LLM (13B) served on mixed T4/P4; target replacement with 30-50% lower p99 latency and lower unit cost.
- Measured during POC: sustained 420 RPS at 512 token average with 65% CPU/GPU utilization on host; KV cache warm-up improved after 45 minutes.
- Tail behavior: p99 increases by 2.5x under bursty parallelism >800 simultaneous sessions; need routing/fallback policy.

Commercial ask: cost model for reserved capacity. AE/SE drafted three commitment scenarios for finance to evaluate:
- Conservative (low commit): 4 A100-equivalent units reserved. Assumptions: 50% utilization steady, 20% headroom for bursts. Effective unit economics: $0.0012 per 1k tokens (tokens counted across generation+context). Break-even vs on-demand at ~60% utilization.
- Base (recommended): 8 A100-equivalent units reserved. Assumptions: 65% utilization steady, automated batching + prefix caching enabled. Effective unit economics: $0.00072 per 1k tokens. Forecast ARR impact: estimated $350k-$600k/yr depending on burst adoption.
- Aggressive (high commit): 12 A100-equivalent units reserved. Assumptions: 80% utilization, canonical batching, priority burst lanes. Effective unit economics: $0.0005 per 1k tokens. High risk if utilization falls below 55%.

Notes on modeling methodology: per-scenario we included: reserved monthly fee (capex-like), marginal on-demand uplift for bursts, expected token volume (derived from instrumentation logs), prefix/KV cache savings (estimated 18-28%), and operational overhead (monitoring, 24/7 support). We provided sensitivity table (drive link) showing unit cost as function of utilization (40%-90%).

SLA / negotiation points to surface with Legal:
- Exact p95/p99 latencies tied to percent of capacity reserved + definition for "burst" and allowed throttling.
- Credits for sustained SLO breaches vs short transient spikes during deployments.
- Runbook & escalation windows for cross-region failover.

Open technical blockers:
- HSM integration timeline - security requires proof-of-concept for key rotation in VPC env.
- Validation of on-prem GPU equivalence for customer's hardware (vendor A100-negotiations ongoing).
- Agreed measurement methodology for "tokens" and caching adjustments (need to standardize tokenization spec).

Next steps (short):
- 2026-03-15: AE to send updated cost workbook (base+conservative+aggressive) with sensitivity bands.
- 2026-03-18: SE + Emberfall infra to validate KMS/HSM flow (demo).
- 2026-03-25: Draft SLA addendum circulated to Emberfall legal for review.

Short-term ask from Emberfall: finance needs per-token unit cost at 65% utilization and a 3-year TCO projection including reserved discount bands.
